title: AI agent vs chatbot: what you are handing over
h1: ai agent vs chatbot: answers, actions and responsibility
description: A plain comparison of asking for an answer and handing over a task, with permission boundaries and a way to decide how much help you need.
answer: a chatbot helps you through conversation; an ai agent can also use tools to carry a task forward. the useful distinction is what you hand over: a question to answer, or a job to do within limits. the names overlap, so ask what access the product gets and what starts the work. an agent can still just chat. adding tools and a schedule also adds decisions about permissions, errors and who checks the result.
og_line: decide what you want to hand over.

them: you want an explanation, a second opinion or a draft that you will use yourself
you prefer to choose and carry out each action after reading the answer
dusk: you need an agent to read permitted material and carry a bounded task through tools
you want a recurring job, and can set its access, stop conditions and review process

compare.h: a working distinction, not two fixed product categories
compare.intro: these columns describe two ways to use ai. the agent column uses dusk bot as the example; other agents differ.

rows.label: what you hand over
cells: a question, passage or idea to discuss
a job, allowed inputs and a clear place for the result

rows.label: who takes the next step
cells: you read the answer and do the next action
the agent may call permitted tools and continue the task

rows.label: access to other apps
cells: for a conversation-only task, you supply the material
may read connected apps or change them, depending on permissions

rows.label: when work starts
cells: you start this exchange by asking
may start in chat, on a schedule or from an app event

rows.label: checking progress
cells: you inspect the reply before using it
in dusk bot, tool activity is shown while the bot works; you can stop it

rows.label: memory and identity
cells: a conversation interface alone says nothing about lasting memory
dusk bots have separate jobs and memory; memory can be turned off

method: we make dusk bot and use its docs to illustrate agent behaviour. we did not run identical tasks through chatbots and agents, and the labels here are working definitions rather than a product ranking. a chat interface can contain tools, memory or background work. check the actual controls before assuming a product fits either column in every situation.

sections.md:
you want help understanding a contract clause, rewriting a paragraph or thinking through a decision. you can paste the relevant material and keep the next action in your own hands. there is no need to connect a whole account just to discuss a small excerpt.

a useful instruction is: "read this paragraph and tell me which terms are unclear. ask me what i mean before rewriting it." you are asking for help with judgement, not handing over authority to change the original document. the [ai agent explainer](/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent) goes further into the vocabulary.

the useful result needs more than a reply to the current message. perhaps you want a review of a folder every friday, with a short note about unresolved questions. an agent with the right file access and scheduling can take on that recurring work. dusk bot routines are created through chat and show their next runs on a card.[^4]

try: "every friday at 3, review the notes in this project folder. list unanswered questions in this chat. do not change the notes, and stay quiet if there are none." [scheduled ai tasks](/scheduled-ai-tasks) covers the point where a repeated prompt becomes a job you need to supervise.

the task still needs a running machine. dusk desktop routines do not run while the computer sleeps or the app is closed. dusk cloud runs them on time.[^4] the word agent by itself does not promise an always-on service.

ask what parts need interpretation. if the same input should always lead to the same action, write that rule down first. if the work needs reading messy notes and deciding what belongs in a summary, describe the judgement you expect and the evidence it should use. neither task needs a vague instruction to "handle everything".

when you give a dusk bot access to connected apps, read-only permissions block actions that change things. sending has its own approval setting. other changes inside an app may not ask first, so keep access read-only or say "ask me before you change anything".[^3] command and file approvals are separate.[^6]

review the first runs and stop if the task grows beyond what you intended. the [computer-control safety guide](/guides/is-it-safe-to-let-ai-control-your-computer) helps you choose a narrow boundary before adding more tools.

faq.q: what are the best uses for an agent in personal life?
faq.a: start with work you can inspect: a recurring review of notes you provide, or a reminder to revisit open questions. define what should be read, where the result goes and when it should say nothing. keep changes out of the first routine rather than granting broad access because the task sounds small.

faq.q: does a chatbot become an agent just because it remembers me?
faq.a: memory and action are different capabilities. dusk bot has a separate memory setting, while app permissions control which tools a bot can call.[^5][^3] ask what the software can do on your behalf, not just what it recalls.

faq.q: do i need a group chat of agents for a simple job?
faq.a: you can start with one bot. dusk bot supports group chats, but the docs recommend keeping groups small and focused.[^7] add another role when you can explain what different work it contributes, such as reviewing assumptions, rather than expecting extra voices to guarantee accuracy.
